title: Trigonometry: Identities, Equations and the Sine and Cosine Rules
seo_title: Year 12 A Level Maths: Trigonometry Worksheets
standard_text: Understand and use the sine, cosine and tangent functions, their graphs, symmetries and periodicity; the sine and cosine rules and the area of a triangle; tan θ = sin θ / cos θ and sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; solve simple trigonometric equations in a given interval.
meta_desc: Free Year 12 A level maths worksheets on trigonometry: exact values, sin² + cos² = 1, tan = sin/cos, solving trigonometric equations in degrees and the sine and cosine rules. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 and tan θ = sin θ / cos θ.
key_sub: Use the graph or CAST diagram to find all solutions in the interval.
body_html:
How it works

Exact values: sin 30° = ½, cos 60° = ½, tan 45° = 1, sin 60° = √3/2. Use sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 and tan θ = sin θ ÷ cos θ to rewrite equations.

To solve sin x = k for 0° ≤ x < 360°: one solution from the calculator, the other is 180° − x.

Example

Solve 2 sin x = 1, 0° ≤ x < 360°.

sin x = ½

30° and 180° − 30°

Answer: 30°, 150°

Common mistakes

  • Giving only the calculator answer.
  • Dividing by sin x and losing solutions where sin x = 0.
  • Using the sine rule for the ambiguous case without checking.

faq.q: How do you find all solutions of a trigonometric equation?
faq.a: Find the first value with your calculator, then use the symmetry of the graph (or the CAST diagram) to find the others in the interval.

faq.q: When do you use the cosine rule?
faq.a: When you know two sides and the angle between them, or all three sides.

items.q: If sin θ = 56 and θ is in the first quadrant, find cos θ.
items.e: cos² θ = 1 − (56)² = 1136, so cos θ = ±√116. In the first quadrant cos is positive, so cos θ = √116.

items.q: Solve 2 cos² x − 3 cos x + 1 = 0 for 0° ≤ x < 360°.
items.e: Factorise like a quadratic in cos x: cos x = 1 or cos x = 12. Solve each one. 0°, 60°, and 300°.

items.q: Solve 2 sin x − √3 = 0 for 0° ≤ x < 360°.
items.e: Isolate the function: sin x = √32. The reference angle has sin = √32. sin is positive in the first and second quadrants, so on one turn the solutions are 60° and 120°.

items.q: Solve 2 cos x + 1 = 0 for 0° ≤ x < 360°.
items.e: Isolate the function: cos x = −12. The reference angle has cos = 12. cos is negative in the second and third quadrants, so on one turn the solutions are 120° and 240°.

items.q: Solve 2 sin x cos x = −√3 cos x for 0° ≤ x < 360°.
items.e: Move everything to one side and factor: cos x(2 sin x + √3) = 0. So cos x = 0 or sin x = −√32. Do not divide by cos x, or you lose solutions. 90°, 240°, 270°, and 300°.

items.q: Solve 2 cos x + 5 = 6 for 0° ≤ x < 360°.

items.q: Solve 2 cos x sin x = √3 sin x for 0° ≤ x < 360°.
items.e: Move everything to one side and factor: sin x(2 cos x − √3) = 0. So sin x = 0 or cos x = √32. Do not divide by sin x, or you lose solutions. 0°, 30°, 180°, and 330°.

items.q: Find θ, where 0° < θ < 180°, if cos θ = −0.9744. Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.
items.e: cos θ is negative, so θ is obtuse. cos−1(−0.9744) = 167.0°.

A triangle has sides 6 cm, 14 cm and 15 cm. Find the largest angle, correct to 1 decimal place.
items.e: The largest angle is opposite the longest side, 15 cm. cos C = (6² + 14² − 15²) ÷ (2 × 6 × 14) = 0.0417, so C = 87.6°.

items.q: Two ships leave a port at the same time. One sails 8 km and the other sails 37 km, and the angle between their paths is 70°. How far apart are they, correct to 1 decimal place?
items.e: Cosine rule: d² = 8² + 37² − 2(8)(37) cos 70°, so d = 35.1 km.

items.e: QR is opposite ∠P and PR is opposite ∠Q. Sine rule: PR ÷ sin 32° = 47 ÷ sin 57°, so PR = 29.7 m.
